front.title: Homing Pigeon Message Protocol, Version 4: The Provable Model

abstract.t: This document specifies version 4 of the Homing Pigeon message protocol. Version 4 defines no new wire format and changes no message of versions 1, 2, or 3. It binds those versions to a formal model of the running implementation: a constraint inventory harvested from the code, a set of numbered properties stated against that inventory, a TLA+ model of each property checked with the TLC model checker, and a conformance suite that holds every model to the code it models. The document states each property, the verdict the checker returned, and the findings where the implementation's behaviour bounds a property's strongest reading, so that a reader can tell exactly which claims about the running software have been machine-checked, and how far each claim reaches.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The Homing Pigeon protocol is specified by three documents. Version 1 defines the message protocol: signed job envelopes, an acceptance gate, key policies, confinement of the work a job can do, and delivery of results. Version 2 records the determinations and shared context the protocol's terms rest on. Version 3 carries the version 1 DTLS 1.3 session profile over email, with the hybrid key agreement group of .

Version 4 answers a different question about the same software: which statements about the running implementation have been proven, in the precise sense that a finite model of the relevant decision has been exhaustively checked, and the model has been held to the code by tests that drive the real decision over its whole input space. This document is that binding. It is a claim about one implementation, the reference runner, at the head its working record names. It is not a claim about every conforming implementation, and Section 10 says plainly what the checking does not reach.

The model's working papers live with the implementation: the constraint inventory, the property files, the TLA+ models and their configurations, the search and checker records, and the conformance suite. This document restates their substance in specification form. Where this document and the working papers disagree, the working papers are the record and this document is in error; the unit tests described in Section 4.4 exist to keep the two from drifting apart unnoticed.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dd.t: A single harvested fact about the implementation: a named value, a fixed behaviour, or a refusal, with the code that carries it and the class of configuration handling it belongs to. Constraints are numbered C1 to C31.
A statement about the implementation, numbered P1 to P13, that a counterexample can be exhibited for. Each property names the constraints it rests on.
A TLA+ specification of one decision the implementation makes, small enough for exhaustive checking, whose states stand in classes the code's inputs fall into.

A checker configuration whose stated invariant is expected to fail, included so that a pass of the main configuration cannot be vacuous: the witness proves the checker can reach the behaviour the property talks about.

A recorded place where the implementation and a property's words, or a model and the implementation, differ. Findings are numbered F1 to F7, and each is stated in the findings section with the resolution that closed it.

section.name: Harvest the constraints first
section.t: The inventory was harvested from the code at a named head: every size cap, every constant the security decisions read, every refusal class, read out of the source and pinned by unit tests that fail when a value changes. A property may only rest on constraints in the inventory, so that the distance between a claim and the code is a list that can be audited.

section.name: State the property so it can fail
section.t: Each property is stated with its counterexample shape: the single observable event that would refute it. A statement that no event could refute is not admitted as a property.

section.name: Write the supposition before the measurement
section.t: For each model, the expected state counts and verdicts are written into the working record before the search or the checker is run. The record then states what was measured against what was predicted. A prediction that fails is itself a finding about the model, the code, or the prediction, and is recorded as one.

section.name: Search, check, and hold to the code
section.t: Each model is treated three ways. First, a twin of the model written in the test suite's language is searched to its fixed point, and the properties are evaluated over every reachable state. Second, the TLA+ model itself is checked with TLC under its main configuration and its witness configurations. Third, a conformance test drives the real code over the decision's whole input space, as far as the code exposes one, and reads the outcomes against the model's. The three treatments must agree; where they cannot, the gap is a finding.

section.name: The pin suite
section.t: Every named value in this document is pinned by a unit test against the code or against the working papers, so that a change to a value the document states turns a test red before it turns this document wrong.

section.name: The Constraint Inventory in Brief
section.t: The full inventory states C1 to C31 with code and test evidence for each. The values the properties below read most directly are these. The maximum job body is 4194304 bytes (C1), the maximum script 1048576 bytes (C2), and the maximum result body 5242880 bytes, with 0 meaning unlimited (C3). A local envelope is capped at 262144 bytes (C4). Signatures are HMAC-SHA-384 (C5) over a shared secret whose estimated entropy is at least 128 bits, a refuse-class startup condition (C6). The one AEAD is AES-256-GCM (C9). The disk guard acts at 90 percent full, keeps the newest 65536 bytes of a truncated live log, leaves workspaces untouched for 3600 seconds alone, and takes at most 512 actions in a pass (C28). The version 3 hybrid group is X25519MLKEM768, group 4588, beside X25519, group 29 (C29). Both ends of a DTLS session run the same side of the framing change, and the replay window is 32768 records (C30). On macOS, confinement at enforce is gated on a probe of the host (C31).

section.name: P1. The acceptance gate
section.t: A job is accepted, and only then run, when every check of the acceptance gate passes, in the gate's stated order: the gate is the only door from a presented envelope to execution. The model is the gate model, checked with TLC under its main and witness configurations, and the claim model covers the gate's final step, the at-most-once claim on a job identifier. Verdict: the invariants hold; the witness configurations fail as designed.

section.name: P2. Result policies cannot widen confinement
section.t: No field of a job or of a result policy can widen the confinement the runner applies: the views a result policy grants are ordered, and the effective confinement is the narrower of what the job asks and what the policy allows. The model is the confinement model, checked at its stated rungs including the production ceiling rung. Verdict: the invariants hold; the witness configurations fail as designed.

section.name: P3. A transport's credentials are a required second gate
section.t: Where a transport has credentials of its own, presenting a validly signed envelope is not sufficient: the transport's credential gate must also pass, and no waiver exists on the DTLS carriage. The model is the transport gate model. Verdict: the invariants hold; the witness configurations fail as designed.

section.name: P4. A named key can do only what its policy allows
section.t: A job signed under a named key is accepted only for the kinds and, where the policy pins one, the exact script the key's policy allows. The models are the key policy model and the composition model, which checks that the gate and the policy decision compose: execution requires both. Verdict: the invariants hold; the witness configurations fail as designed.

section.name: P5. Replay cannot re-execute
section.t: Execution is at most once per job identifier: a replayed envelope, however it is presented, does not run the job a second time. The model is the replay model, with the claim model at the gate's final step. Verdict: the invariants hold; the witness configurations fail as designed.

section.name: P6. Refuse-class configuration behaves as required
section.t: A present but unusable value in the refuse class of settings stops the runner at startup, and the error names the setting that cost the start. The model is the decision model. Verdict: the invariants hold; the witness configurations fail as designed. Finding F5 recorded the one place the code's naming fell short of this property, at the secret floor; a weak additional key is now refused under its own setting's name, and the finding is closed.

section.name: P7. The disk guard cannot stop the runner
section.t: When the disk under the runner's state directory measures at or over 90 percent full, a guard pass gives up only the runner's own material, in the order of C28, records what it did, and the runner continues: no pass terminates the runner, follows a symlink, or touches the pending outbox, the configuration, or the security event log. The model is the disk guard model: 160 distinct states under search, its invariants holding in every one, and TLC returns the same count with no error. The witness configurations fail as designed. Findings F1, F2, and F3 bounded this property and are closed: the model now measures as the code does, a removal is recorded whatever it freed, and a measurement that fails ends the pass. F2 and F3 were differences from the property's own words, closed in the runner; F1 was a difference of the model, closed in the model.

section.name: P8. A v3 session that can agree the hybrid group does so
section.t: When the client offers the hybrid share and the server's carriage profile carries the hybrid option, the agreed group is 4588, the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid, not X25519 alone. A hello offering no group the profile can select is refused. The model is the hybrid selection model: 16 distinct states under search, its invariants holding in every one, and TLC returns the same count with no error. The conformance drives the real client and server cores through 4 handshakes, every combination of offer and profile, and the negotiated group is the model's outcome on all 4. The witness configurations fail as designed.

section.name: P9. No session is claimed across the framing break
section.t: Both ends of a DTLS session run the same side of the framing change of C30, and no document of this protocol presents a session across the break as supported. This property is a claim about what the documents claim, so it is held by a pin that reads them, not by a checker model: the framing record states that mixed-version DTLS interoperability is not supported across the landing, and the support matrix claims no mixed-version session.

section.name: P10. On macOS, enforce means the probe passed
section.t: For every start on macOS with confinement in enforce mode, either the probe of C31 passed on that host or the runner does not start; there is no weaker run. The gate the startup asks is one gate for the 3 platforms that have a confinement backend of their own, darwin, freebsd, and win32, and the model states the claim for all 3; the index states it for macOS. The model is the probe gate model: 288 distinct states under search, its invariants holding in every one, and TLC returns the same count with no error. The conformance drives the real gate over all 144 starts the model stands in, and the gate's answer is the model's on every one. The witness configurations fail as designed.

section.name: P11. A result body leaves within max_result_bytes, down to the fitting's floor
section.t: When max_result_bytes is set to a non-zero value, the body that is signed and sent is at most that many bytes, down to the fitting's floor, and a cut is marked result_truncated; under a result's floor the body leaves at the floor, over the cap and marked. The model is the result fitting model: 12 distinct states under search, the marking and unlimited and fitting invariants holding in every one, the floor invariant with them, and TLC returns the same count with no error. The configuration that states the cap with no floor is expected to fail, at exactly one class: finding F7. The fitting cannot cut below the size of its own last pass, the fixed envelope plus both streams at their first and last 2 KiB; for a result with 40000 bytes on each stream that floor is 4625 bytes, and a cap under the floor gets the body at the floor's size, over the cap, marked. The marking is honest and the signature covers what is sent. Finding F7 is closed by the floor standing in the property's words; nothing in the runner changed.

section.name: P12. A local envelope over the cap is refused unread
section.t: An envelope over 262144 bytes on the local path is refused before any verification work, at both doors of the path: the inbox scan reads at most one byte past the cap, a symlink is refused unread, and the loopback listener reads at most one chunk past the cap before the same check. The model is the local gate model: 200 distinct states under search, its 4 invariants holding in every one, and TLC returns the same count with no error. The conformance drives the real doors over 112 arrivals in 140 runs at the real cap, counting the bytes read at the door itself and standing in for the verifier: nothing over the cap reaches it, and an envelope of exactly the cap goes through. The witness configurations fail as designed. Finding F6 recorded that a file whose cut at the cap falls inside a character was refused with the reason that it is not UTF-8. The scan now reads the size of what it read before it decodes anything, and a file over the cap is refused as too large wherever its cut falls; the finding is closed.

section.name: P13. The runner does not start on a weak secret
section.t: For every start, every key in the key map, the default and the additional keys alike, estimates at or over 128 bits of entropy, or the start refuses. The model is the secret floor model: 67 distinct states under search, its invariants holding in every one, and TLC returns the same count with no error. The conformance builds the real key map over every standing of 3 keys, 125 configurations, and the start is the model's on every one. The witness configurations fail as designed. Finding F5 recorded that a refusal caused by a weak additional key named the default key instead: the refusal was right, and the name was wrong, in 32 of the 107 refused configurations. The refusal now names the key under its own setting's name, on all 107 refusals, and the finding is closed.

section.name: The Findings
section.t: The model work stated 7 findings. All 7 are closed, each in the place its difference lived: F2, F3, F5, and F6 in the runner, F1 and F4 in the model and its files, and F7 in the property's words. Each remains held by a test as the tree stands, so a change on either side, the code's or the words', shows as a test change.

dd.t: The disk guard model ended a pass sooner than the code does. The code measures again at the door of the next class, and a pass can continue where the model stopped. Closed in the model: it now measures as the code does, before every action and again at the door of every class, and every pass the real guard can make ends on one of the model's finished passes.

Material of 0 bytes was removed by the disk guard with no record, against P7's clause that every acting pass leaves an event. Closed in the runner: the guard notes a removal when the path is gone, whatever it freed, and an event names exactly what a pass removed.

A disk measurement that fails in the middle of a guard pass was taken as over, and the pass continued giving up material, against P7's clause that a later class is touched only while the disk measures at or over the threshold. Closed in the runner: a measurement that fails ends the pass, and nothing is given up without a measurement that says the disk is at or over the threshold.
The disk guard model once had no witness configurations in its own files. Closed by adding them.

A weak additional key was refused in the default key's name, against P6's clause that the error names the setting that cost the start. Closed in the runner: the key is refused under its own setting's name, and the naming holds of the real key map on all 107 refusals.

A file cut inside a character at the local cap was refused as not UTF-8, though it is UTF-8 read whole and its fault is its size, against P12's clause that the recorded reason is the envelope's. Closed in the runner: the scan reads the size of what it read before it decodes anything, and a file over the cap is refused as too large wherever its cut falls.

A result cap under the fitting's floor sends the body over the cap, marked, against P11's words as they stood. The floor is a property of the fitting's last pass, not of any one result. Closed in the property's words, by the owner's decision: P11 now holds down to the fitting's floor, and under the floor the body leaves at the floor, over the cap and marked; the runner is unchanged, and a marked result over the cap stands.

section.name: Operational Considerations
section.t: The model is a model of decisions, not of the whole program. Each model abstracts one decision into the classes its inputs fall into, and the conformance suite is what ties a class back to the inputs it stands for. An operator should read a verdict as: this decision, over the inputs the classes cover, behaves as the property states, except where a finding says otherwise. Values in the inventory change as the code changes; the pin suite is the mechanism that keeps this document honest between revisions, and a deployment that changes a pinned value has changed the claims of this document whether or not the document has been reissued.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests no IANA action. It defines no new registrations, code points, or parameters. The group value 4588 for X25519MLKEM768 is registered by and is only cited here.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: The security value of this document is the precision of its claims. A property that has been checked is stated with the model that checks it and the count of states the checker examined, and the findings state where the implementation fell short of a property's strongest reading, and how each such place was closed: in the runner, in the model, or in the property's own words. A reader deciding how much to trust the runner should weigh the findings as part of the protocol's security posture, not as footnotes to it.

The checking itself has limits. The models are finite abstractions written by the same hands as the code, and a mistake shared by both is invisible to the conformance suite; the witness configurations guard against vacuous passes, not against a wrongly drawn class boundary. The checker examines the model, not the compiled program. The claims of this document are therefore claims of checked models held to the code by tests, which is a stronger position than untested assertion and a weaker one than a proof of the program itself, and the document asks to be read as exactly that.
